text:
Welcome to Issue 87 of the weekly developer tooling roundup.

Every week we go through new releases, updates, and side projects and pick out the useful ones, so you don't have to do the searching yourself. This week we have five links, and three of them deserve a closer look.

The first is a new Rust linter. It's for you if you want stricter checks than your current setup gives you, or clearer explanations when something gets flagged. It tries to catch subtle mistakes early while keeping false alarms down.

The second is a Git GUI. Plenty of us live in the terminal, but sometimes it's faster to see branches, diffs, and history laid out on screen. This one is built for speed and has a clean layout.

The third is a tracing tool. If you've ever tried to work out where the time goes in a request, this one follows execution across your system and shows you where the bottlenecks are.

The last two links are smaller finds that we think you'll enjoy.

Thanks for reading, and welcome to everyone who just joined. There are 9,400 of you now.
